_comment: Promotional video ideas for a minimal / deep tech artist starting at zero followers. Each idea is a testable format, not a one-off: 'hook' is the literal on-screen text for the first 1.5 seconds, 'shots' is the shot list, 'goal' is the single metric it is built to move. Ideas are deliberately weighted toward formats that earn saves and shares, because those convert strangers into followers far better than likes do.

categories.hook_lab: Attention mechanics — the first two seconds, tested in isolation
categories.groove_science: The thing only you can teach: swing, shakers, pocket, space
categories.production_teardown: Deconstruct a track or a technique, front to back
categories.gear_dawless: Hardware, one-take jams, tactile and hypnotic
categories.sound_design: Turning objects and field recordings into the palette
categories.scene_culture: The world around the music — clubs, labels, records, rituals
categories.series_identity: Repeatable formats that make people follow rather than like
categories.meme_relatable: In-jokes that only the niche gets, which is the point
categories.release_promo: Selling a track without sounding like you are selling a track
categories.experiments: Higher-risk formats worth two attempts each

ideas.title: The 3-frame proof
ideas.hook: you are hearing 3 shakers, not 1
shots: Cold open on the waveform of a single shaker hit, huge on screen
Solo each of the three layers for 1.5s with a hard cut
ideas.why: Opens with a claim the viewer can immediately test against their own ears. No greeting, no logo, no 'hey guys'.
ideas.cta: Which layer did you not hear?

ideas.title: Stop doing this
ideas.hook: stop quantising your hats to 100%
shots: Grid on screen, hats locked, groove sounds stiff
ideas.why: A prohibition hook outperforms a suggestion hook because it implies the viewer is currently making the mistake.
ideas.cta: Save this before your next session

ideas.title: Wait for the bar-16 turn
ideas.hook: wait for bar 16
shots: Loop plays, timer counting bars in the corner
At 16 the bassline enters and the hats drop out
Hold on the crowd/hands or the meter reacting
ideas.why: An explicit countdown gives the algorithm a reason to keep the viewer past the 3-second cliff, and gives the viewer a reason to rewatch.

ideas.title: Nobody tells you
ideas.hook: nobody tells you minimal is a mixing genre
shots: Talking to camera in the studio, 4 seconds max
Cut to the mixer, show 6 tracks with tiny fader moves
End on the loop playing with your hands off everything
ideas.why: 'Nobody tells you' promises insider knowledge; the payoff must arrive by second five or the hook is a lie.
ideas.cta: Follow — this is part of a series

ideas.title: One sample, whole track
ideas.hook: this entire track is one sample
shots: Reveal the source: a coffee grinder, a lift door, a lighter
Rapid-fire show each element derived from it
ideas.why: Transformation hooks are the strongest format in music short-form. The gap between source and result is the entire payload.

ideas.title: Do you hear it?
ideas.hook: 9 out of 10 people can't hear this
shots: Reveal the difference visually — one automation lane
ideas.why: A challenge hook drives comments, and comments early in a reel's life are the cheapest signal you can manufacture honestly.
ideas.cta: A or B in the comments

ideas.title: The 400ms loop
shots: No text at all — open on the loudest, most tactile moment of the groove
Hold a single locked-off shot of hands on gear
Loop the video so the last frame matches the first
ideas.why: A seamless loop turns one view into three. Some of your best-performing posts should have no hook text at all, so you can measure whether text is helping.

ideas.title: Price-tag contradiction
ideas.hook: this groove cost £0
shots: Reveal it is all stock plugins / a free sample pack / one phone recording
Show the plugin list on screen
ideas.why: Anti-gear content reaches the largest possible slice of the producer audience — the ones who own nothing.

ideas.title: Swing ladder
ideas.hook: same loop at 50, 54, 58, 62% swing
shots: Static overhead of the screen or gear
Four cuts, one per swing value, 3s each, value huge on screen
End on your favourite with 'this one'
ideas.why: Comparative content is the single most saveable thing a groove-focused artist can make, and swing is the literal identity of the genre.

ideas.title: The ghost note lesson
ideas.hook: the note you're not playing is the groove
shots: Add ghost notes at -18dB, show the velocity lane
A/B them with a hard cut
ideas.why: Names a concept most bedroom producers have felt but cannot articulate. Naming things is what makes people follow a teacher.
ideas.cta: Part 2: ghost notes on the bassline

ideas.title: Subtract until it grooves
ideas.hook: i deleted 6 tracks and it got better
shots: Delete tracks one at a time on camera, counter on screen
ideas.why: Minimal's core value is restraint. Showing subtraction as an active craft is on-brand and rare — everyone else adds.

ideas.title: One-bar vs two-bar
ideas.hook: why your loop gets boring at bar 8
shots: Play a one-bar percussion loop, let it become annoying
Extend to two bars with one variation
Extend to four with a second variation
ideas.why: Solves a specific, felt pain. Pain-solving content gets saved; entertainment content gets liked.

ideas.title: The offbeat shaker
ideas.hook: put the shaker where you think it shouldn't go
shots: Move it to the late 16th, show the grid
ideas.why: A single, copyable move the viewer can try in 60 seconds. Copyability is what drives the save.

ideas.title: Kick and bass as one instrument
ideas.hook: stop eq-ing your kick and bass separately
shots: Solo kick, solo bass, both sound fine
Sidechain + one EQ dip, show the analyser clean
ideas.why: The most common technical failure in the genre, demonstrated visually with a meter so the claim is verifiable on a phone speaker.

ideas.title: Groove template steal
ideas.hook: i extracted the groove from a 1998 record
shots: Show the groove/swing extraction in the DAW
Apply it to your own drums
ideas.why: Shows a workflow most people do not know exists and ties your content to genre lineage.

ideas.title: Silence as percussion
ideas.hook: the best percussion hit is nothing
shots: Mute a full beat on the turnaround
Show the crowd/meter reaction or just let it breathe
ideas.why: A philosophical point delivered in 12 seconds. Positions you as someone with taste, not just technique.

ideas.title: Track in 5 layers
ideas.hook: every element, one at a time
shots: Build up: kick, then hats, then bass, then stab, then texture
All together for the last 4 seconds
ideas.why: The most reliable evergreen format in producer content. Works for any track you make, forever.
ideas.cta: Which layer is doing the work?

ideas.title: Rebuild a classic
ideas.hook: recreating the groove from [classic] in 60 seconds
shots: Build your version live, sped up
ideas.why: Borrows the recognition of a known record. Use short reference clips and always credit the original in the caption.

ideas.title: Loop to arrangement
ideas.hook: from 8 bars to 6 minutes
shots: Timeline zoom-out showing the full arrangement
Scrub through the arrangement, hitting each section for 1s
ideas.why: Arrangement is where most minimal producers stall. Showing the map is worth more than showing the loop.

ideas.title: The 3-plugin chain
ideas.hook: 3 plugins, that's the whole chain
shots: Add each plugin with the setting visible, one cut each
ideas.why: Constraint content is inherently shareable and answers the 'what do I actually need' question beginners are stuck on.

ideas.title: Fix my bad loop
ideas.hook: this loop is bad. here's why
shots: Play a genuinely mediocre loop of yours
Diagnose on screen with three text callouts
ideas.why: Self-critique is disarming, builds trust fast, and gives you infinite content because bad loops are free.

ideas.title: What 20 hours of mixing looks like
ideas.hook: same track, 20 hours apart
shots: Show the project file's version history
ideas.why: Process content proves effort. It converts casual viewers into people who feel invested in your releases.

ideas.title: The stab autopsy
ideas.hook: one piano note becomes this
shots: Add chorus, then a filtered delay, then a plate, then bit reduction
ideas.why: The dub chord is a signature sound of the genre. Owning the tutorial for it makes you the person people associate with it.

ideas.title: Reverse engineer a 30-second clip
ideas.hook: someone asked how this was made
shots: The result next to the original
ideas.why: Answering a public request builds a visible feedback loop, which is the mechanism that makes people comment on future posts.

ideas.title: One-take, one-machine
ideas.hook: one machine, one take, no edits
shots: Let it run — no cuts at all
ideas.why: Hands-on-hardware footage is inherently hypnotic and performs well even with no hook text. Cheapest high-retention footage you can make.

ideas.title: The £80 setup
ideas.hook: the whole setup cost £80
shots: Pan across a deliberately cheap rig
Price tags on screen per item
ideas.why: Directly attacks the gear-acquisition anxiety that dominates the producer audience. High share rate.

ideas.title: Blind test: hardware vs plugin
ideas.hook: one of these is £1200. one is free
shots: The reveal at the very end
ideas.why: Built for comments — people cannot resist guessing — and the reveal at the end drives full watch-through.

ideas.title: The one knob
ideas.hook: this one knob is the whole track
shots: Close macro shot of a filter or delay-feedback knob
Slow sweep with the loop playing
Pull back to reveal the setup
ideas.why: Macro shots of hands and knobs are the most 'scrollable-stopping' image in electronic music content.

ideas.title: Patch from nothing
ideas.hook: no samples. building a kick from a sine
shots: Pitch envelope, then click layer, then saturation
ideas.why: Synthesis-from-scratch content is deeply saveable and demonstrates real skill in under 30 seconds.

ideas.title: Broken gear jam
ideas.hook: this sampler is broken. that's the sound
shots: Show the fault — a stuck key, a bad output, a dying battery
Build a groove that uses the fault
ideas.why: A story and a sound at once. Character-driven content is what people follow; technique alone is what they save and forget.

ideas.title: Desk tour, but honest
ideas.hook: the 3 things i actually use
shots: Point at the unused gear, then dismiss it
ideas.why: Inverts the aspirational studio-tour genre. Contrarian versions of saturated formats out-perform straight ones.

ideas.title: Jam in a weird place
ideas.hook: making a track in a stairwell
shots: Establish the location — car park, train, beach, stairwell
The loop, with the location's ambience recorded into it
ideas.why: Location gives an ordinary jam a reason to exist. Also naturally supplies the field recording for the track.

ideas.title: Object of the week
ideas.hook: today's percussion: a bike chain
shots: Record the object on a phone, close up
ideas.why: A repeatable series with infinite supply. Series formats convert viewers to followers because they promise a next episode.

ideas.title: City to shaker
ideas.hook: i recorded a train and made a hi hat
shots: Field recording, on location, headphones on
ideas.why: The transformation gap — noise into music — is the strongest single mechanic in sound-design content.

ideas.title: Resample until it's unrecognisable
ideas.hook: 5 rounds of resampling
ideas.why: Shows a genuinely genre-defining technique with a clear visual counter that keeps people watching to the end.

ideas.title: The room is an instrument
ideas.hook: i played the loop into my bathroom
shots: Speaker in a tiled room, mic on a stand
Blend it in, A/B against the dry
ideas.why: Physical, tangible, cheap. It shows craft without requiring anyone to own software.

ideas.title: Noise floor as a texture bed
ideas.hook: silence is not empty
shots: Solo the 'silence' — a tape hiss, a room tone, vinyl crackle
Show it under the loop, then mute it
Unmute — the track feels alive again
ideas.why: Teaches a subtle idea that separates amateur minimal from professional minimal. Highly saveable.

ideas.title: One-shot from a voice note
ideas.hook: my friend's voice note is now the lead
shots: Play the original voice note (permission first)
ideas.why: Personal, funny, and shows a technique. Content with another human in it out-performs pure gear content on shares.

ideas.title: Dub delay throw, explained
ideas.hook: how to throw a delay without ruining the mix
shots: Show the send automation and the feedback grab
ideas.why: A live-performance move that looks like magic and takes ten seconds to teach.

ideas.title: Sample the sample pack you hate
ideas.hook: worst sample pack i own, one usable sound
shots: Find one hit, mangle it hard
ideas.why: Constraint plus humour. Also reframes 'I don't have good sounds' as an excuse, which is a shareable idea.

ideas.title: The 30-second blend
ideas.hook: watch the two records lock
shots: Overhead of the decks, both records visible
The blend happening, EQ moves visible
Hold on the moment the new groove takes over
ideas.why: Overhead deck footage is the most recognisable image in the culture. Keep it to the single best 30 seconds of the set.

ideas.title: Empty room set
ideas.hook: nobody came. played anyway
shots: One person walking in and starting to dance
ideas.why: Vulnerability plus persistence. This is the kind of post that gets shared to stories by people who have been there.

ideas.title: The 6am selection
ideas.hook: 6am. one record left.
shots: The floor reacting, phone held low
ideas.why: Time-of-night is the entire mythology of the genre. Lean into it.

ideas.title: Bag reveal
ideas.hook: 5 records i'm not playing tonight, and why
shots: Pick each up, one sentence each, 3s cuts
ideas.why: Selector-as-curator content builds taste credibility, which is what gets you booked, not just followed.

ideas.title: Read the room in real time
ideas.hook: the floor emptied. here's the fix.
ideas.why: Teaches DJing as a skill rather than a pose. Rare content, very high save rate among aspiring DJs.

ideas.title: Three decks, one groove
ideas.hook: the third deck is just a shaker loop
shots: Close on the third deck's contribution, solo it
ideas.why: Technical spectacle that is specifically minimal — layering percussion live is genre-native, not generic DJ content.

ideas.title: Booth POV
shots: Camera at eye level in the booth, no text
Slow pan from the mixer to the floor
Hold on the crowd for the last third
ideas.why: No-hook, atmosphere-only post. Include one or two of these a week as a control against your text-heavy posts.

ideas.title: Practice mix, unglamorous
ideas.hook: this is what practising actually looks like
ideas.why: Failing on camera is the fastest trust-builder available and costs nothing to produce.

ideas.title: Record shop haul
ideas.hook: £40 in a second-hand shop
shots: Each record, 3s of the best bar
ideas.why: Digging content carries built-in nostalgia and gets shared by labels and shops, which is free reach from accounts bigger than yours.

ideas.title: Explain the genre to an outsider
ideas.hook: explaining rominimal to someone who hates it
ideas.why: Two-person content reaches outside your niche while staying about the niche. Great top-of-funnel post.

ideas.title: One label, one minute
ideas.hook: the label that defined this sound
shots: Three key releases, one bar each
Why it mattered, one sentence on screen
ideas.why: Educational scene content attracts the older, deeper part of the audience — the people who actually buy records and book DJs.

ideas.title: Club etiquette, minimal edition
ideas.hook: 3 things nobody does at a proper minimal party
shots: Three quick vignettes, staged and funny
ideas.why: In-group humour signals membership. People share this to say 'I am one of these people'.

ideas.title: The queue at 4am
shots: Documentary footage — queue, breath in cold air, a door
No commentary, just ambient sound and your track underneath
ideas.why: Atmosphere posts carry your music without pitching it. Use your own unreleased track as the audio.

ideas.title: Vinyl vs USB, settled
ideas.hook: the honest answer about vinyl
ideas.why: A mild, genuine opinion on a settled-seeming debate drives comment volume without making enemies.

ideas.title: Festival field notes
ideas.hook: 5 things i learned at [festival]
shots: End on the best 5 seconds of music you heard
ideas.why: Event-tagged content rides an existing surge in search and hashtag traffic during and just after the event.

ideas.title: The 20-year-old record that still clears floors
ideas.hook: released in 2003. still unbeatable.
shots: Drop the needle on the best 8 bars
Your reaction / the crowd if you have it
ideas.why: Legacy-record posts get shared by the artist, the label, and the collector accounts. Free distribution.

ideas.title: Loop a day
ideas.hook: loop 47 of 365
shots: Same framing every single time — this is the point
Same end card with the number
ideas.why: A visible counter is a promise of continuity. It is the single most effective follow-driver available to a new account, and it forces you to post daily.

ideas.title: One sound, one week
ideas.hook: day 3: still only using this shaker
ideas.why: A constraint series generates a week of content from one decision and gives viewers a reason to return.

ideas.title: Finish my track
ideas.hook: you decide the next element
shots: Next episode opens with the winner
ideas.why: Turns comments into a mechanic rather than a request. Each episode's audience has a stake in the next.
ideas.cta: A or B — highest voted wins

ideas.title: Weekly track ID
ideas.hook: the best minimal record i heard this week
ideas.why: Curation is a legitimate way to post daily without needing to produce daily, and it builds relationships with the artists you feature.

ideas.title: Bedroom to booth
ideas.hook: week 6 of trying to get my first gig
ideas.why: A documented arc gives strangers a reason to care about you specifically rather than about the technique. Arcs are what build a real following.

ideas.title: Rate my loop
ideas.hook: rate this 1-10, be honest
shots: Score overlay from last week's post
ideas.why: Explicitly asks for the comment. Low effort, high comment rate, and the feedback is genuinely useful to you.

ideas.title: Sunday reset
ideas.hook: closing the week's session
shots: The best thing you made this week
Next week's one goal on screen
ideas.why: A calm, weekly ritual post gives your grid rhythm and reads as a person rather than a content machine.

ideas.title: The archive dig
ideas.hook: opening a project file from 2021
ideas.why: Infinite supply from your own hard drive, and it demonstrates growth, which is a story people follow.

ideas.title: POV: wrong lineup slot
ideas.hook: pov: you play minimal at 9pm
shots: Empty room, you playing something delicate
Cut to the next DJ, big room, packed
ideas.why: Specific in-group pain. The narrower the joke, the harder the niche shares it.

ideas.title: 47 shakers
ideas.hook: me adding the 47th shaker
shots: Screen full of near-identical percussion tracks
Solo two of them — inaudible difference
ideas.why: Self-deprecating genre humour. Costs one screen recording.

ideas.title: The promoter request
ideas.hook: "can you play something people know?"
shots: You playing a 9-minute rominimal cut anyway
ideas.why: Every DJ in the genre has received this message. Recognition drives the share.

ideas.title: Explaining it at Christmas
ideas.hook: my family asking what kind of music i make
shots: Play 8 bars of minimal to a blank face
ideas.why: Reaches beyond the niche because the situation is universal while the music stays yours.

ideas.title: The USB check
ideas.hook: checking my usb for the 6th time
shots: Repeated identical shots of you plugging it in
One shot of it actually failing
ideas.why: Physical comedy with no dialogue, which travels further than talking-head humour.

ideas.title: Track title generator
ideas.hook: how minimal artists name tracks
shots: Spin a wheel of nouns: 'Untitled', a Greek letter, a number
Generate three absurd but plausible titles
Show one of your real ones
ideas.why: Affectionate mockery of the genre's conventions. Signals you are inside the culture, not selling to it.

ideas.title: The 5am philosopher
ideas.hook: the guy who explains the groove to you at 5am
shots: Cut to black on the punchline
ideas.why: Character comedy is memorable and gets quoted in comments, which extends the post's life.

ideas.title: Demo folder reality
ideas.hook: opening my 'nearly finished' folder
ideas.why: The most relatable producer pain there is. Pairs well with a follow-up tutorial on finishing tracks.

ideas.title: The 8 bars that sold it
ideas.hook: this is the part the label replied to
shots: Screenshot of the reply, name blurred
ideas.why: Sells the track by telling a story about it instead of announcing it. Announcements do not travel; stories do.

ideas.title: Made-of teardown for the new track
ideas.hook: everything in the a1, in 40 seconds
shots: Layer-by-layer build of the actual release
ideas.why: Turns a promo post into a tutorial. People save tutorials; they scroll past promos.

ideas.title: Test press moment
ideas.hook: first time hearing it on vinyl
ideas.why: Genuine emotion, one take, no production required. Among the highest-performing posts an underground artist can make.

ideas.title: Play it out before it's out
ideas.hook: testing the unreleased one on a real floor
ideas.why: Social proof beats self-promotion. Someone else's reaction is more persuasive than your description.

ideas.title: The version that didn't make it
ideas.hook: the b-side that got rejected
ideas.why: Gives you two posts from one release and invites disagreement, which is comment fuel.

ideas.title: Artwork process
ideas.hook: how the sleeve got made
shots: The final sleeve next to the record
ideas.why: Reaches the design-interested audience and gives your release a second, non-musical angle.

ideas.title: One year later
ideas.hook: this track did nothing for 11 months
shots: The moment it got picked up
ideas.why: A story about patience — deeply resonant for anyone at zero, and it recirculates an old release.

ideas.title: Free loop pack drop
ideas.hook: the shakers from the ep, free
ideas.why: Trades value for a follow and a comment. The most honest growth mechanic there is — you are actually giving something away.

ideas.title: Loop swap
ideas.hook: we swapped 8-bar loops. here's what happened
ideas.why: Posted by both accounts, it exposes each of you to the other's audience — the fastest legitimate growth mechanic for a small account.

ideas.title: Duet the diagnosis
ideas.hook: someone asked me to fix their loop
ideas.why: Free content supplied by your audience, and everyone whose loop you fix becomes an advocate.

ideas.title: Interview a record shop owner
ideas.hook: asked a shop owner what actually sells
ideas.why: Borrows an institution's credibility and gets reposted by the shop. Local, real-world reach.

ideas.title: Feature a smaller artist
ideas.hook: this account has 200 followers and better grooves than me
ideas.why: Generosity to people smaller than you builds the network that will carry you later, and it is the kind of post people screenshot.

ideas.title: Two producers, one sample
ideas.hook: same sample. two completely different tracks.
ideas.why: Structurally interesting and doubles the distribution. Works with anyone, at any level.

ideas.title: Answer the DM in public
ideas.hook: someone asked how to start with £0
ideas.why: Every DM you receive is a content prompt, and answering publicly signals that you actually reply.

ideas.title: Guest selector takeover
ideas.hook: gave my account to a friend for 60 seconds
ideas.why: Cross-audience exposure with almost no production cost, and it makes your account feel like a place rather than a feed.

ideas.title: Remix open call
ideas.hook: here are the stems. go.
ideas.why: Creates content from other people and a reason for them to tag you. Follow up by featuring the best entries.

ideas.title: Silent reel
ideas.hook: watch this with the sound off
shots: Visual-only rhythm — a metronome, a light, a hand
Text describing what you would be hearing
Turn the sound on for the last 3 seconds
ideas.why: Most people scroll muted. A reel that works muted and then rewards unmuting is a genuinely different bet worth testing twice.

ideas.title: 90-second deep dive
ideas.hook: the long one: why minimal is hard to mix
shots: No hard cuts — one continuous explanation
ideas.why: Long-form has lower reach but far higher follow-per-view. Post one a week and judge it on follows, not views.

ideas.title: Text-only cold open
ideas.hook: i have made 200 loops and finished 3 tracks
shots: Full-screen text for 2 seconds, no music
ideas.why: Breaking the expected pattern — silence and text where music is expected — is a legitimate way to stop the scroll.

ideas.title: The 6-second loop
ideas.why: Tests whether pure rewatch count can carry a post with no hook, no text and no face. Cheap to make, worth knowing.

ideas.title: Reply-to-comment video
ideas.hook: answering the comment that annoyed me
ideas.why: Comment-reply videos inherit the parent post's audience and reliably generate more comments.

ideas.title: Same reel, two hooks
ideas.hook: (post the identical video twice, 5 days apart, different first 2s)
shots: Version B hook on the repost
ideas.why: The only clean way to measure your own hook writing. Log both results in the tracker and compare — this is the experiment that improves everything else.

ideas.title: No-music reel
ideas.hook: the studio at 3am, no music
shots: Room tone only — hum, traffic, a fan
One note at the very end
ideas.why: Atmosphere without a track. Tests whether your audience is there for you or only for the loops.

ideas.title: Carousel-to-reel repost
ideas.hook: the 5 rules, now as a video
shots: Take your best-performing carousel or static post
Rebuild it as a reel with the same content
ideas.why: Recycling proven content into the format with the most reach is the highest-leverage thing you can do with a small back catalogue.
